title: Introduce tenant-bound KMS sandbox and audit clarity shim
author: Nora Patel
description: Motivation: Several customers with strict residency and audit requirements reported intermittent KMS denials and noisy audit envelopes when operator-scoped keys were used for feature preview environments. This PR introduces a tenant-scoped ephemeral KMS sandbox allocator plus an audit-clarity shim that standardizes audit headers, reduces noisy provenance fields, and surfaces deterministic residency claims to downstream processors. Design summary: 1) kms-sandbox service (new): a lightweight allocator that provisions short-lived, tenant-bound CMK aliases and returns a signed usage assertion. Allocator enforces region affinity, tenant entitlement checks, and per-tenant rate limits. 2) audit-clarity middleware (runtime): canonicalizes audit headers on the request path (tenant_id, claimed_region, kms_alias, operator_tag) and emits an audit_fingerprint header to support downstream dedupe and aggregation. 3) RBAC v2 bindings: new policy templates that map sandbox aliases to least-privilege service roles and an operator-fence rule that denies cross-tenant alias reuse. 4) Fallbacks: when sandbox allocation fails, requests can opt-in to a read-only fallback using pre-approved multi-tenant read keys; write operations are blocked by default. Backwards compatibility: the shim is opt-in by default for Hosted customers; Dedicated and Private deployments can enable via console flag or config map. No runtime changes to public API surface (generation/embeddings calls same endpoints) — behavior only differs in underlying key selection and audit headers. Security considerations: sandbox keys are short-lived (TTL default 30 minutes) and bound to a cryptographic attestation signed by the allocator. Keys cannot be exported; KMS provider plugins enforce never-export policy. The RBAC templates include explicit deny rules for cross-tenant operations and operator impersonation vectors. Migration and rollout: staged rollout plan with shadow mode (emit audit_fingerprint but do not block), followed by soft enforcement for a subset of traffic, and full enforcement after 2 weeks of telemetry. We added observability hooks: metrics redwood.kms.sandbox.alloc_latency, redwood.audit.fingerprint_count, and an alert rule to detect allocation failure rates >1% per hour. Tests: unit tests cover allocator policy checks, rate limiting, signed assertion format, and header canonicalization. Integration tests added to perf-canary to validate allocation under burst load and to verify audit dedupe behavior. CI: added a new integration job (integration/kms-sandbox) to the pipeline; all checks pass in this run. Files changed: mostly allocator service (cmd/kms_sandbox), middleware (runtime/audit_clarity.go), rbav templates (rbacv2/templates/tenant_sandbox.yaml), docs (docs/security/kms-sandbox.md), and e2e test harness updates. Related work: builds on ENG-3917 (policy-enforcer refactor) and is complementary to ENG-4123 (residency-assertor). Known limitations: sandbox allocator currently supports AWS and internal mock-KMS; GCP/Azure providers are planned (ENG-4381). Upgrade notes: stateful clusters should migrate alias metadata; migration helper included at tools/kms_sandbox/migrate_aliases.go. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Docs updated - [x] Linear issues referenced

release_notes: Added tenant-scoped KMS sandbox allocator and audit clarity middleware. Introduces opt-in tenant sandboxing for short-lived keys, audit fingerprinting for dedupe, RBAC templates for cross-tenant deny rules, and new observability metrics. Rollout is staged (shadow -> soft enforce -> full).
